67564221.ds_scopenote: A hereditary autosomal dominant disease characterized by increased plasma and urinary CORTISOL, resistance to adrenal suppression by DEXAMETHASONE, and the absence of clinical stigmata of CUSHING SYNDROME. Symptoms are variable but may include HYPOGLYCEMIA; HYPERTENSION, and metabolic ALKALOSIS; CHRONIC FATIGUE SYNDROME, and ANXIETY. In females, overproduction of adrenal ANDROGENS may cause INFERTILITY, ALOPECIA (male pattern bladness) HIRSUTISM, and menstrual irregularities. Caused by mutations in the NR3C1 gene. OMIM: 615962
